name: Insider Threat
description: Malicious or negligent insider — data theft, sabotage, policy violation.
initialKeyQuestions: Who is the subject of investigation and what is their role?
What data or systems did the subject access outside their normal scope?
Were large file copies, USB transfers, or cloud uploads observed?
Did the subject access systems after a resignation or termination notice?
Are there signs of data staging or collection before departure?
What communication channels (email, Teams, Slack) were used?
Was account or credentials sharing observed?

initialNextSteps.action: Preserve all relevant logs before the subject's access is revoked or systems are modified
initialNextSteps.rationale: Evidence destruction risk is highest while the subject is active
initialNextSteps.pointer: SIEM, DLP, proxy, badge-access, M365 UAL, endpoint logs

initialNextSteps.action: Pull full DLP and data-loss alerts for the subject's accounts over the investigation window
initialNextSteps.rationale: DLP alerts are the primary signal for data staging and exfiltration
initialNextSteps.pointer: DLP console, Microsoft Purview, CASB file-activity report

initialNextSteps.action: Collect endpoint forensic triage (KAPE or Plaso) from the subject's workstation
initialNextSteps.rationale: Surfaces file access history, USB device connections, recent files
initialNextSteps.pointer: KAPE targets: USB, LNK files, JumpLists, MFT, SRUM

initialNextSteps.action: Establish the subject's normal access baseline for the 3 months before the window
initialNextSteps.rationale: Anomalous access is only meaningful relative to a baseline
initialNextSteps.pointer: SIEM query: same user, same resource types, prior quarter

synthesisHint: This is an insider-threat case — prioritize T1052 Exfiltration Over Physical Medium (USB), T1567 Exfiltration to Cloud Service, T1078 Valid Accounts (the insider's own), and T1056 Input Capture.
